exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

I want cottage cheese with live and active cultures. Which brand should I choose, and why?
reviewed_answer:
Choose Good Culture—specifically Good Culture Simply 2% Low-Fat Classic Cottage Cheese or the 4% version. It is explicitly made with live and active cultures, and it was the top-rated cottage cheese in a 2026 Wirecutter taste test for its creamy texture, tender curds, and balanced tang.

Why Good Culture fits your goal

Live and active cultures: Its ingredient list includes live and active cultures, including Lactobacillus paracasei.

Strong independent reviews: Wirecutter named its Simply 2% and Simply 4% Classic varieties its top picks, attributing the tangy flavor to live probiotic cultures.

Simple formulation: It is marketed as having simple ingredients, high protein, and no artificial ingredients.

Good taste and texture: Independent taste testing also ranked Good Culture highly, praising its curd size, moisture level, and tang.
allrecipes

What to buy
If you want	Pick
Lower fat, still creamy	Good Culture Simply 2% Low-Fat Classic Cottage Cheese 

Richer, more traditional dairy flavor	Good Culture Simply 4% Milkfat Classic Cottage Cheese 

A more yogurt-like, tangy option	Nancy’s Organic Probiotic Low-Fat Cottage Cheese 
Label-check tip

At the store, confirm the tub says “live and active cultures” in the ingredient list; avoid relying only on phrases like “probiotic” or “cultured.” Good Culture is the clearest mainstream U.S. choice because its cultures are listed directly and its product quality is consistently well reviewed.
